tips.li: Colonists eat when they're hungry, not all at once, so a dining room can manage with a seat for most of them rather than every one.
Someone who finds every chair at the table taken eats without one, and loses mood for it.
The dining room is the room everyone sees once or twice a day: the colony's best furniture and art pay off most there.
The planner keeps the turn, the style and the materials when you switch to a larger size of the same room.
Small bedrooms beat a big barracks for mood: even a narrow room with a bed and a lamp is a room of one's own.
Bedrooms built side by side share their walls, so a row of them takes less than the figure given here.
Ascetics don't mind a barracks; leave them a bed there if they like it.
The old barracks makes a fine guest room, workshop or rec room once everyone has moved out.
Hospital beds improve tend quality and immunity gain; a vitals monitor beside them raises surgery success further.
A clean floor keeps a room cleaner, and a clean hospital means fewer infections.
Upgrading a built room plans only the pieces that are missing; nothing already there is moved.
A game keeps two or three people busy at most. A big colony needs several, and of different kinds.
Recreation comes in kinds (social, gaming, cerebral, dexterity and more), and each tires of being used: variety keeps the need full.
A rec room next to the dining room means colonists relax right after eating instead of walking across the map.
